title: Chapter 29: Xiao Wan, Doctor Skull-cracker
html:
The door clicked shut behind them, and the small sound seemed unnaturally final in the silence.

“He San, based on what happened last time, what should we do first?”

“Find the exit as fast as possible.”

…

After securing the entrance, Chen Ge called Xu Wan and asked her to meet him in the props room.

“Boss, what’s the rush? The visitors are already inside, aren’t they?” Xu Wan hurried over in her ghost-bride costume and stage makeup from Minghun.

“There’s a new scenario on the third floor called Murder by Midnight. Those medical students are going to be our first proper test group.” Chen Ge opened the props room and checked the black phone for the new reward.

“Shouldn’t park management inspect a new scenario before we open it?” Xu Wan lifted the hem of her long costume so she would not trip. “And what exactly are you looking for?”

“A new costume for you.”

“Costume?”

At the back of the room sat a familiar wooden box—the same kind that had once contained the rag doll and black phone. Inside were a heavy-looking doctor’s robe, a strange theatrical prop, and a yellowed missing-person notice.

“Found it.” Chen Ge lifted the robe. It looked like ordinary hospital clothing at first glance, but decorative chains had been sewn into the fabric, making it much heavier than expected. Distorted faces had been worked into the metal links.

“Boss, this is the costume you made for me?” Xu Wan instinctively took a step back. Even as a prop, it looked deeply unpleasant. “Do I have to wear it?”

“You’re an actor in a Haunted House, Xiao Wan. Think of what your drama teachers told you: an actor has to commit to the role.” As Chen Ge spread out the robe, a grotesque theatrical mask slipped from its folds. Even he had not realized it was included. He picked it up and stared at it for a moment.

The mask had been designed to resemble several mismatched faces joined into one. Its deliberately crude construction made it more disturbing, not less.

“Please don’t tell me that goes with the costume too.” Xu Wan had already retreated to the doorway.

“Just try it once so I can see the complete effect. I’ll take the monster role next time, I promise.” Chen Ge clasped his hands in exaggerated pleading.

“Fine. Once.” Xu Wan took the mask and robe and stepped aside to change out of her ghost-bride costume. When she returned, she looked down at herself and sighed. “Boss, your definition of a uniform needs work.”

With the chains, oversized robe, and mask in place, her entire silhouette changed. The cheerful employee Chen Ge knew had vanished beneath a genuinely unsettling stage character.

“Not bad.” Chen Ge decided not to let her look in the mirror yet. “Here, this prop completes it.”

He handed her the lightweight theatrical prop that had come with the costume. It was designed to look heavy and menacing on camera, but its hollow construction made it suitable for performance.

Xu Wan had long since accepted that her boss’s ideas operated by their own logic. She simply nodded and took it.

“Keep your phone where you can hear me through the earpiece. We’ll stay in contact while the visitors are inside.”

“We?” Xu Wan looked over at him. Her normal voice sounded strangely eerie through the mask. “You’re entering the scenario too?”

“Of course. Come on. Our guests are probably getting bored.”

Chen Ge sent Xu Wan into Murder by Midnight while he returned to the control room. Within minutes he located all seven students on the monitors. Despite their earlier bravado, they were moving cautiously enough to make their nerves obvious.

They’re still near the entrance after all this time? I may need to encourage them a little.

He changed the background track to Black Friday and called Xu Wan.

“Xiao Wan, this scenario spans parts of all three floors, and it’s easy to lose your bearings. Stay in contact and follow my cues so we don’t accidentally cross paths at the wrong time.”

“Understood.”

After ending the call, Chen Ge applied some stage makeup and entered through a staff passage. The black phone allowed him to trigger the scenario’s theatrical effects from his interface, giving Murder by Midnight far more flexibility than Minghun or Night of the Living Dead.

Inside the darkened set, a concealed staff entrance opened behind one of the room props. Chen Ge emerged, restored the set dressing, and moved on.

“Xiao Wan, they should be near Room 207. Wait by the left stairwell until I call you.” Chen Ge let his eyes adjust to the darkness, then headed toward the upper level by a separate staff route.

The medical students had no idea the performers were moving into position. They were still examining props and searching the rooms for anything that looked like a clue.

“Other than the darkness and the cold, this place isn’t that frightening. Are we being too cautious?” Monkey, the shortest and most talkative of the group, glanced around. “Brother Feng, let’s split into two teams. We’ll cover the rooms much faster.”

The tall student everyone called Brother Feng had been uneasy when their preparations for Minghun proved useless, but the longer they remained in the new scenario without incident, the more his confidence returned. “That makes sense. Monkey and Lao Song, take the two girls and search the rooms on the left. The three of us will take the right.”

“We should have split up from the start. I don’t know why everyone is acting so nervous. Compared with the anatomy labs at school, this place is practically relaxing.” The speaker was a young woman with dyed hair and light makeup. Compared with Gao Ru Xue’s reserved appearance, she carried herself with a little more swagger.

“Sister Hui, Brother Feng, I really think we should stay together.” He San hovered near the middle of the group, visibly unhappy with the plan. “You haven’t seen what this boss does when he gets an idea. Normal logic does not apply to him.”
